text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Saviour-97, a military exercise involving ten countries, began on Monday at the Krivolak range in central Macedonia. President Kiro Gligorov said all countries, regardless of their size, must cointribute to peace and stability.

- Macedonian Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski received Liberal Party leader Petar Gosev, who demanded early elections this autumn and a government of experts to prepare them. Crvenkovski replied that the government could be appointed or dismissed only by the parliament.
- IMRO-DPMNY, the biggest opposition party, hopes to assemble 50,000 people at a mass protest in Skopje on May 15 at which it will demand the resignation of the government and early elections.
- The ethnic Albanians' PDP, part of the government coalition, came out against the planned protest rally on May 15 in Skopje, while the opposition PDPA supports it but will not take part.
- The opposition Liberal Democrats and other smaller parties also support the IMRO-DPMNY's demands, but will not take part in the Skopje rally.
- The conservatives (MAAK) and the Democratic Party believe early elections are the only way to save an economy they say is in total collapse.

- Macedonia and FR Yugoslavia have almost completed work on defining their mutual border. They will also sign a special agreement on the protection of cultural and historical monuments. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
